Yeah, it's the same. And, while it depends on the technology, often times you are also even saving it - go to your temporary internet files and for some of the sites you're streaming from you'll probably find lots of *.flv files that you just 'streamed'. The main constraint is downloads obviously have to be in-order and the backing technology needs to be able to started or stopped from anywhere so a form of compression that relied extensively on what happened last frame, without lots of 'real' frames inserted throughout, would not fly. As a practical matter streams also generally have very heavy compression. A raw 1080p 24 frames per second film uses 1920x1080x24x24, or 1,194,393,600 bits, of data per second. In other words - 1195Mbps or 1.2 gigabit per second. What you get on a blu-ray is a heavily compressed version of that. What you get on a stream is a super super extremely heavily compressed version of that compression. And that's just for 1080p at 24FPS...
